name: Citizen Service Number (BSN)
issuer: the municipality where the person is registered
note: Netherlands's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: a natural person's TIN (the Citizen Service Number, BSN) is allocated at birth or at registration with the municipality; 9 digits, the ninth a check digit by an eleven-weighted modulus the sheet spells out, which the game doesn't compute yet (`check` left out; adding it to checks.ts would let it). Read as given at birth by the municipality, to residents. No fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Netherlands: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Natural persons: At birth or at registration at the municipality ... The Dutch TIN has 9 digits: 999999999. ... N9 is a check digit. ... The Citizen Service Number (BSN)
